Audience & Segmentation — Primary eligible population: all North America contacts with documented, product‑category promotional opt‑in per the "Email & Privacy Standard – Promotional Consent Clarification." Within that consented population we will prioritize two tiers: Tier A (Sales‑priority High‑Value) = opt‑in + high‑intent signals (premium feature trial in last 90 days, historical spend in top 20%, or ICP‑matching usage patterns); Tier B (Broad Active Opt‑ins) = opt‑in + engagement with any Acme communication in the last 12 months but without Tier A signals. Contacts lacking documented opt‑in for this product category are excluded from promotional sends for AcmePlus. 

Cadence & Schedule — First six weeks (intensive launch window): Tier A: up to 3–4 AcmePlus touches per week (mix of promotional offers, clear pricing/value messaging, trial conversion nudges, and serviceable transactional follow‑ups); Tier B: capped at 1–2 touches per week with messaging focused on clear value and pricing (no teaser/bait language) and lower creative repetition; after six weeks cadence moves to a sustained nurturing rhythm (Tier A: 1–2/week; Tier B: 1 every 1–2 weeks) subject to performance and complaint thresholds. All sends will honor immediate AcmePlus opt‑out and global unsubscribe rules (one‑click opt‑out for AcmePlus-specific messaging, logged consent provenance, and access to the preference center to downgrade cadence), and personalization will use only data elements permitted by the attached policy; any deviation or higher-frequency rollout for Tier B is documented as a trade‑off requiring executive sign‑off.

rounds.response:
Audience & Segmentation — Primary eligible population: North America contacts with documented, product‑category promotional opt‑in per the "Email & Privacy Standard – Promotional Consent Clarification"; within that consented base we prioritize Tier A (High‑Value revenue focus: opt‑in + high‑intent signals such as premium trial in last 90 days, top‑20% historical spend, or ICP usage patterns) and Tier B (Broad Active Opt‑ins: opt‑in + engagement with any Acme communication in the last 12 months). Tier A is the primary revenue engine; Tier B is a core growth engine for volume and will be run with education‑forward, clear‑pricing messaging and tighter quality controls to protect sales leads. 

Cadence & Schedule — Launch window (weeks 0–6): Tier A up to 3–4 AcmePlus touches/week (clear pricing/value, trial conversion, and serviceable transactional); Tier B default set to 1–2 touches/week (education + explicit pricing) and may be scaled toward the modeled performance envelope (up to 3 touches/week, per the updated "AcmePlus Email Channel Targets – NA Launch" workbook) only if real‑time monitoring shows complaint/unsubscribe rates and Sales quality metrics remain within the thresholds in "Email & Privacy Standard – Complaint & Unsubscribe Benchmarks"; after week 6 cadence moves to sustain (Tier A 1–2/week; Tier B 1 every 1–2 weeks), personalization limited to policy‑permitted data, every send includes one‑click AcmePlus opt‑out and logged consent provenance, and subscribers may downgrade cadence via the preference center. 

Monitoring & Enforcement — Daily/weekly monitoring of complaint rate and unsubscribe rate, and weekly tracking of conversion, early churn, and sales no‑show; crossing Compliance thresholds triggers immediate throttling (≥50% cadence reduction) and a mandated cross‑functional review for rollback or remediation. 

Key Decisions & Trade‑offs — (a) Baseline: consent‑anchored plan with Tier A (3–4/week) and Tier B default 1–2/week with conditional ramp; (b) Marketing preferred variant: Tier B treated as launch‑level 3–4/week to maximize modeled growth; (c) Compliance/Sales concerns: inclusion of non‑consented contacts (not allowed), complaint/unsubscribe risk, and lead quality/early churn impact; (d) Reconsideration triggers: complaint/unsubscribe above Compliance benchmarks, material sales‑quality degradation (early churn/no‑shows), or explicit executive sign‑off to expand cadence.
